newsitem.title: USA: MGM Grand Inc president backs Q3 forecast.
newsitem.headline: MGM Grand Inc president backs Q3 forecast.

text.p: MGM Grand Inc President Alex Yemenidjian said he was comfortable with analysts' consensus earnings forecast of $0.42 a share in the third quarter.

"I feel comfortable with the Street consensus, which is $0.42. That's a number I wouldn't forget," Yemenidjian told Reuters after a speech at the Salomon Brothers Gaming and Lodging conference in Las Vegas.

The company, along with its 50 percent partner Primadonna Resorts Inc, has scheduled the official opening of their New York, New York hotel for January 3, but Yemenidjian said the casino would be ready to open as early as December 15.
"We'll have our friends and employees there to make sure the property is really seasoned for a proper opening," Yemenidjian said.

With such a "soft opening," as it is known in the casino industry, MGM plans to work out any kinks in the hotel and gambling operations before regular visitors begin arriving at the resort, which is built on a New York City theme.
The 2,035-room hotel costs MGM and Primadonna $460 million to build. Salomon Brothers analyst Bruce Turner expects it to generate $289 million in revenue in its first full year.
Earlier, Primadonna Chief Financial Officer Craig Sullivan said the companies expected New York, New York to generate $90 million in cash flow next year.

Six months after the opening, the partners will have the opportunity to bid for each other's stake in what Yemenidjian termed a "Texas shoot-out". Both companies "would like to own 100 percent" of New York, New York, he added.
MGM continues to be active outside the United States, considering possible new operations in Mexico, Argentina, Canada and South Africa, he said.
